_how_to_use: Copy this file, fill in every field, and run: python analyse.py cases/<your_file>.json. Keys starting with '_' are ignored. State in 'provenance' whether each value is published or assumed, and where it comes from.
name: my_site
description: One sentence: what the site produces and what the stream loads represent.
reference: Full citation of the source of the stream data.
_stream_file_format: CSV columns: stream, type (hot/cold), T_in_C, T_out_C, dT_shift_K, and ONE of Q_<unit> (e.g. Q_kW, Q_kWh_per_t) or CP_<unit> (e.g. CP_kW_per_K). Latent loads: use a 1 K temperature interval.
_ambient_T_C: Ambient temperature [°C]. External (non-process) heat pump sources must be at or below it.

heat_pumps._eta_lorenz: Lorenz efficiency, 0 < eta <= 1. 0.55 is from Padullés et al. (2026); justify any other value.
heat_pumps._source_T_C: Default heat source temperature on the T* axis. Use the process cooling level below the pinch, or ambient.
heat_pumps._sink_levels: Candidate sinks, sized automatically from the GCC from lowest to highest. 'gcc_max' = isothermal sink at the highest GCC temperature. A level may set its own T_source_C.
heat_pumps._eta_lorenz_sensitivity: Optional: further Lorenz efficiencies; heat pumps are re-sized and re-costed for each.

_basis: Optional. {'type': 'power', 'operating_hours_per_year': h} for loads in kW/MW, or {'type': 'per_product', 'production_per_year': x, 'production_unit': 'hl'} for loads such as kWh/hl. Use null if unknown: no annual figures are then reported.

sources.prices: cite the price source, period, band and tax basis (example values: Eurostat Portugal 2026-S1, electricity band ID, gas band I3, excl. VAT)
sources.heat_pump_cost: Danish Energy Agency catalogue (2025) by sink temperature (sheets 1.1 / 2.a / 2.b), with its add-ons for lift above 75 K and steam generation (isothermal sinks); remove the steam add-on if the heat pump heats air or water directly. Padullés et al. (2026, Table 3) is fitted to brewery heat pumps (below the catalogue above about 1.7 MW)

hp_dea_1_1.source: Danish Energy Agency, Technology Data - Industrial Process Heat (2025), 'Nominal investment (*total)' 2025, equipment + installation, per MW of heat output, sheet 1.1 'Heat pump, up to 60 °C, temp. lift 40 K': 0.95 M€/MW (0.91-0.95), unit size 0.5-5 MW. O&M (DEA 2025) sheet 1.1: fixed 2,127 EUR/MW/y, variable 3.07 EUR/MWh

hp_dea_2a.source: Danish Energy Agency, Technology Data - Industrial Process Heat (2025), 'Nominal investment (*total)' 2025, equipment + installation, per MW of heat output, sheet 2.a 'High-temperature heat pumps up to 125 °C': 1.2 M€/MW (0.9-1.5), unit size 0.3-25 MW. O&M (DEA 2025) sheet 2.a: fixed 2,494 EUR/MW/y, variable 3.6 EUR/MWh

hp_dea_2b.source: Danish Energy Agency, Technology Data - Industrial Process Heat (2025), 'Nominal investment (*total)' 2025, equipment + installation, per MW of heat output, sheet 2.b 'High-temperature heat pumps up to 150 °C': 1.55 M€/MW (1.25-1.8), unit size 0.5-80 MW. No catalogue sheet above 150 °C: units with hotter sinks are costed with this sheet as an extrapolation (flagged). O&M (DEA 2025) sheet 2.b: fixed 2,494 EUR/MW/y, variable 3.6 EUR/MWh

dea_lift_2a.source: Danish Energy Agency, Technology Data - Industrial Process Heat (2025), 2025 values, sheet 2.a: 'Additional equipment cost for temperature lift above 75 K' 0.15 M€/MW (0.05-0.25)

dea_lift_2b.source: Danish Energy Agency, Technology Data - Industrial Process Heat (2025), 2025 values, sheet 2.b: 'Additional equipment cost for temperature lift above 75 K' 0.2 M€/MW (0.1-0.3)

dea_steam.source: Danish Energy Agency, Technology Data - Industrial Process Heat (2025), 2025 values, sheets 2.a and 2.b: 'Steam generation increases equipment cost by' 0.2 M€/MW (0.05-0.3); applied to isothermal sinks (steam). The sheets' COP penalty for steam (-0.15) is not applied: COP comes from the Lorenz model

_economics: Optional; needs 'basis'. Any key left out takes the default in pinch/economics.py (DEFAULTS, each with its source). For a 'power' basis, operating_hours_per_year must match the basis. heat_recovery_equipment: list of [kind, size] (kinds: hr_tank [m3], heat_pump/mvr/electric_boiler [kW]) to evaluate a site without heat recovery. scenarios: {name: {parameter: value}} re-runs the full design, RQ1 and RQ3 with those overrides. Heat pumps: cost function chosen by sink temperature (heat_pump_cost_classes) plus add-ons (heat_pump_cost_adders); O&M per cost function (fixed_om_EUR_per_unit_year, variable_om_EUR_per_MWh).
_screening: Optional plausibility thresholds; defaults and their sources are in pinch/design.py.
_area_targeting: Optional (step 3). Film coefficient per stream in kW/(m2 K); exchanger cost per unit a + b (A/N)^c in EUR, with source. If no sourced cost law exists, set cost_law to null and give a sweep of installed area cost (a = 0, c = 1). Needs 'basis' and 'economics' (loads are converted to kW; hot-utility cost from gas price / boiler efficiency).
